plan.reason: Redis is a single stateful dependency on the cart and checkout paths. A pod kill directly tests restart recovery, persistent-state usability, and whether dependent customer operations fail during recovery.

prediction.summary: Cart reads or writes and checkout requests may fail or incur elevated latency during Redis recreation. Persistent storage should preserve cart contents after recovery; any lost cart items or failed post-fault business checks would confirm the suspected vulnerability.

plan.reason: Cartservice has one pod and is a direct dependency of both frontend and checkoutservice. This distinguishes cartservice availability loss from the Redis state/recovery failure tested in V1.

prediction.summary: Cart operations and checkout requests requiring cart data are expected to produce customer-visible errors or latency substantially above the approximately 60 ms baseline p95 until cartservice is recreated.

plan.reason: Paymentservice is a single critical checkout dependency. A sustained service outage tests customer impact independently of restart/state-loss behavior and distinguishes payment-path failure from cart-path failure.

prediction.summary: Checkout payment attempts should fail or become substantially slower while paymentservice is unavailable, while non-payment traffic may remain available.

plan.reason: Frontend is the single customer entrypoint. A pod kill tests whether its readiness and recreation behavior preserves customer access, without relying on target unhealthy_count, which would be tautological for this fault.

prediction.summary: Users may experience elevated request failures or latency while the sole frontend pod is recreated; checkout and other backend capabilities should recover once the entrypoint is ready.

replan_note: No prior experiments exist, so all candidates are untested. The plan prioritizes the critical stateful cart dependency first, then the single cartservice dependency, payment path, and customer entrypoint. It uses both pod_kill and pod_failure to distinguish restart/recovery behavior from sustained dependency unavailability. Results from V1 will determine whether later cart-related failures are primarily Redis state/recovery issues or cartservice availability issues; results from V3 and V4 will establish whether checkout or the entire site is more sensitive to single-pod loss.
